name: Parque Principal
description: The central plaza is Jardin's social and practical hub: wooden rocking chairs spill out from cafe terraces, vendors sell coffee and sweets, and the basilica anchors one side. Guesthouses, restaurants, banks, and tuk-tuk stands cluster within a block or two, making it the default base for short stays and the easiest spot for casual cafe work.
bestFor: first-time visitors, short stays, cafe workers
pros: Best cafe options for wifi and coffee
Constant people-watching and easy transport links

name: Basilica District
tagline: Steps from the candy-colored neo-Gothic landmark
description: The streets immediately surrounding the Basilica Menor de la Inmaculada Concepcion mix quiet residential blocks with small family-run shops and a handful of guesthouses set back from the busiest plaza corners. It offers a calmer version of the central experience, close enough to walk everywhere but a notch removed from the loudest evening chatter.
bestFor: travelers wanting proximity without plaza noise
pros: Close to the plaza but quieter at night
Strong sense of traditional town life
Easy access to church events and local markets

name: Alto de las Flores Road
tagline: The climb toward the cable car and mountain views
description: Heading uphill from town toward the teleferico station, this stretch mixes a few guesthouses and cafes with increasingly open views over the valley. It's less commercial than the plaza but still walkable, and the cable car ride from here up to Alto de las Flores is one of Jardin's signature short excursions for panoramic photos.
bestFor: views, morning walks, travelers wanting separation from the center
pros: Easy access to the cable car

name: Vereda La Salada (Coffee Farm Country)
tagline: Working coffee farms just outside town
description: A short jeep or tuk-tuk ride from the plaza, this rural vereda is dotted with working coffee fincas, waterfalls, and trails leading toward the cock-of-the-rock reserve. Stays here are rustic and nature-focused rather than convenient, suited to travelers who want to experience the harvest and countryside up close rather than town amenities.
pros: Close to waterfalls and the bird reserve
cons: Requires transport into town for most errands
Wifi and amenities are minimal to nonexistent
